definitions.gloss: together; along with; at the same time
definitions.explanation: Doing something jointly with another person or combining things in the same action or location.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I ate lunch together with my friend.

examples.japanese: {書類|しょるい}は{領収書|りょうしゅうしょ}と{一緒|いっしょ}にファイルに{入|い}れておいてください。
examples.english: Please put the documents in the file together with the receipt.

notes:
One of the most frequently used adverbs in Japanese. {一緒|いっしょ}に can describe people doing things jointly, objects being placed in the same location, or events occurring simultaneously.

The particle と is commonly used with {一緒|いっしょ}に to specify the companion: Aと{一緒|いっしょ}に (together with A).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}く: to go together
- {一緒|いっしょ}に{食|た}べる: to eat together
- {一緒|いっしょ}に{住|す}む: to live together
- {一緒|いっしょ}に{働|はたら}く: to work together
- {一緒|いっしょ}に{遊|あそ}ぶ: to play together

USAGE:
In casual speech, {一緒|いっしょ}に is sometimes shortened to just {一緒|いっしょ} (without に). The expression {一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}こう (let's go together) is a common way to invite someone along.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {共|とも}に: together — more formal and literary
- {連|つ}れ{立|だ}って: together, in company — implies physically going somewhere as a group
- {合|あ}わせて: combined, together — focuses on adding things together rather than companionship
